entries.clue: The numbered day you write at the top of a letter
Only a day ago, and already forever out of reach
Last thing to fade from the bough, a mouth with no face behind it
Shrill summons set the night before to haul you out of bed
One of the twelve; thirty days, give or take a couple
January to December: one lap of the sun, taking 365 days and a quarter
Ornate park canopy where brass players parp through a Sunday afternoon
Frilly paper mat placed under a cake for no practical reason at all
Milliner for whom it is always six o'clock and always time for tea
Long-eared tea-table host whose springtime madness is proverbial
Stall game of tossing wooden rings over a prize nobody ever quite wins
Fete drum of folded tickets; you win a tin of beans
Unanswered question comparing a raven with a writing desk
